prompt: Collect every signup problem instead of failing on the first: validate returns a list of messages and validateOrThrow turns a non-empty list into one IllegalArgumentException.
explanation: Throwing on the first bad field tells the user about one mistake at a time; gathering the problems into a list and reporting them together is far friendlier. Each rule is an independent if statement -- not else-if -- so several can fire for the same input, and the order of the ifs fixes the order of the messages. validateOrThrow keeps the two jobs separate: validate decides what is wrong, and only the caller-facing method decides that being wrong is an exception.
hints: Use three separate if statements, not else-if -- a signup can break more than one rule.
name.trim().isEmpty() catches a name of only spaces, and email.indexOf('@') < 0 is true when there is no at sign. Test for null first so neither call blows up.
In validateOrThrow, return early when the list is empty; otherwise build the joined message with a StringBuilder (or String.join("; ", problems)) and throw IllegalArgumentException.
